messages:
marta (support): heads-up — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spikes on text-generation endpoints since ~02:00 UTC. topline: 3x p95 and intermittent 504s. first alert came from acct: acme-inc. No config changes on their side.

alice (eng-runtime): thanks — do we have a correlation with deploys or infra changes around 02:00?

infra-bot: deploy: infra/gpu-driver-update pushed to us-west2 at 01:58 UTC by ben.

ben (eng-infra): that was the staged host kernel + driver bundle (linux-5.19 + nvidia-driver-535). rolled to canary then to svc pool at 01:58. I can roll back but want telemetry first.

carla (eng-sre): checking traces now. initial look: tail latency for 16k token requests jumps and we see NVMe queue depth rising on affected hosts. logs show repeated nvme timeout messages on a subset of hosts.

marta (support): customers also saw billing ingestion delays (logs delayed) and some auth refresh 502s when backends timed out. customer is pushing high concurrency, so they surface SLO failures fast.

alice (eng-runtime): can you paste a snippet of the nvme errors?

carla (eng-sre): paste from host gpu-11: "nvme nvme0: I/O 1234 QID 8 timeout, aborting command" followed by repeated resubmits. dmesg shows: "nvme0: I/O 0xabc1234 timeout, resetting controller"

ben (eng-infra): that matches a known pattern when driver+kernel combo changes NVMe IO scheduling behavior. NVMe controller resets can cause short stalls that blow up p99 for workloads with many small IOs (checkpoint writes, model KV flush).

alice (eng-runtime): interesting — our runtime does a lot of small KV cache persisting (every 100 tokens) on local NVMe. If resets happen during token generation, that adds tail latency. Question: did the driver update change NVMe interrupt affinity or IO queue depth defaults?

ben (eng-infra): yes. The 535 driver has a new default NVMe driver interaction for MSI-X vectors. It exposed a pathological path on some firmware combos. We saw similar once in staging but not at production scale.

marta (support): customer's timeline: spikes started ~02:05 UTC, matches rollout. They're on dedicated capacity in us-west2. They want a mitigation ASAP — something to stop 504s.

carla (eng-sre): mitigation options: 1) roll back driver to previous version on affected pool, 2) enable nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us or change nvme queue settings, 3) move high-IO customers to unaffected pool (slow but safe).

alice (eng-runtime): runtime-level mitigations we can apply immediately: reduce KV persist frequency (disable checkpointing for live requests) and increase request timeouts + retry logic to mask transient NVMe stalls. I can push a hotfix toggle to runtime config to skip `persist_checkpoint` for the next 30m. That will reduce small writes but slightly increase cold-recover time if host dies.

ben (eng-infra): I'll start rollback on a small subset (3 hosts) to validate. If rollback fixes it we can do a wider rollback. Rolling back the driver takes ~8 min per host (drain, reboot).

carla (eng-sre): also running a quick health-check script across nodes: `for h in $HOSTS; do ssh $h "dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i nvme"; done` and `iostat -x 1 5` to spot queue depths.

marta (support): I'm telling the customer we're investigating and will provide a mitigation in 15m. They asked if there's a known workaround besides waiting for rollback.

alice (eng-runtime): push toggle now — `/toggle persist_checkpoint=false --scope=us-west2-pool` — deploying in 30s. This will require a runtime config broadcast; not a restart. Should be immediate for new connections.

infra-bot: config change applied to us-west2-pool at 02:20 UTC by alice.

carla (eng-sre): after toggle, early telemetry shows p95 down ~30% on affected nodes, p99 still elevated but fewer 504s. NVMe resets still present on some hosts though.

ben (eng-infra): rollback started on host gpu-11 (one of the worst offenders). I'll report back when complete.

marta (support): customer confirms some improvement, still seeing occasional timeouts on long sequences. They asked whether we can route them away from impacted hosts while we finish rollback.

carla (eng-sre): quick routing plan: mark impacted hosts as `maintenance` in the scheduler so new requests won't land there. Existing requests will finish. Ben, can you mark hosts offline?

ben (eng-infra): doing maintenance toggles now for hosts with repeated nvme resets. Command: `infra-admin set-host-state gpu-11,gpu-12 maintenance`. Applied.

alice (eng-runtime): scheduler respects maintenance flag within ~15s. We'll see rebalancing.

carla (eng-sre): monitoring: p99 for the customer dropped from 12s to 3.5s after maintenance + toggle. NVMe faults reduced on remaining online hosts. Looks much better but keep an eye for regressions.

ben (eng-infra): rollback on gpu-11 done. boot logs show driver reverted to 530 and no NVMe timeouts since reboot. Planning to continue rollback in 5-host batches.

marta (support): customer wants RCA and ETA for full fix. ETA request: how long for full rollback or vendor patch?

ben (eng-infra): rollback across the pool will take ~90m to finish if we do 5-host parallel batches safely. Vendor patch unknown; upstream driver team working but we have a safe rollback.

alice (eng-runtime): after rollback completes we should revert the persist_checkpoint toggle. We'll also schedule a follow-up to consider async batching for KV writes to reduce small IO.

carla (eng-sre): action items: ben continue rollback and update every 15m; alice keep toggle and prepare revert; marta update customer 15m cadence; I'll keep monitoring p95/p99 and NVMe errors.

marta (support): sent initial customer update — letting them know we've applied mitigation and are rolling back driver, next update in 15m.

ben (eng-infra): 02:44 UTC rollback batch 2 started (hosts gpu-13..gpu-17).

carla (eng-sre): note for postmortem: include kernel/driver combo, NVMe firmware versions (some affected hosts share firmware 1.2.3-rc), and our KV persist IO pattern. Also include guidance for staging rollout checks (fio mixed small IO to simulate KV pattern).

alice (eng-runtime): quick repro steps for later: run repeated generation with concurrency 8 and sequence length 8k, run fio on local NVMe with `--rw=randwrite --bs=4k --iodepth=32 --numjobs=4` simultaneously and watch for `nvme timeout`.

marta (support): customer appreciates the fast mitigation. I'll keep them informed. thanks team. :heart:

carla (eng-sre): continuing to monitor — will post final once pool rollback completes and p99 stable for 30m.

ben (eng-infra): update 03:15 UTC — rollback ~80% complete, affected hosts showing normal nvme behavior, p99 back to baseline for most customers.

carla (eng-sre): final check: p99 stable for 35m, NVMe resets gone. Marking incident as mitigated. We should open a postmortem doc and link firmware/drivers to the change.

marta (support): closing loop with customer and creating postmortem ticket in PM system. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
